items.followUp: State two parts of the cell theory.

rubric.why: Award for stating that living organisms are made of cells or that the cell is the basic unit of life.
rubric.description: Living organisms are made of cells, and the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
rubric.how: Look for either the composition of organisms from cells or the cell being the basic unit.

rubric.why: Award for stating that new cells come from cells that already exist.
rubric.description: New cells arise from pre-existing cells.
rubric.how: Look for the origin of new cells from existing cells.

modelAnswer: All living organisms are made up of one or more cells.
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
New cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

items.followUp: Define endocytosis and name its two types.

rubric.why: Award for defining endocytosis as the membrane enclosing substances and bringing them into the cell.
rubric.description: The plasma membrane folds around substances and encloses them in a vesicle to bring them into the cell.
rubric.how: Look for uptake of substances through the enclosing action of the plasma membrane.

rubric.why: Award for naming both types of endocytosis.
rubric.description: The two types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.
rubric.how: Both type names must be present.

modelAnswer: Endocytosis is the process by which the plasma membrane folds around substances and encloses them in a vesicle to bring them into the cell.
Its two types are phagocytosis and pinocytosis.

items.followUp: State two reasons why organisms are classified.

rubric.why: Award for stating that classification makes organisms easier to identify or study.
rubric.description: Classification organizes organisms into groups, making them easier to identify and study.
rubric.how: Look for easier identification or study of organisms.

rubric.why: Award for stating that classification helps compare organisms or show their relationships.
rubric.description: Classification shows similarities and differences among organisms and their relationships.
rubric.how: Look for comparison of characteristics or relationships among organisms.

modelAnswer: Classification organizes organisms into groups, making them easier to identify and study.
It helps show similarities and differences among organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: How does community participation help conserve forests and wildlife?

rubric.why: Award for identifying protection of Himalayan forests or wildlife habitats as a role of the project.
rubric.description: The project helps conserve biodiversity by protecting Himalayan forests and wildlife habitats.
rubric.how: Look for forest or habitat protection.

rubric.why: Award for mentioning local community involvement or sustainable management.
rubric.description: The project encourages local communities to participate in conservation and sustainable forest management.
rubric.how: Look for community participation or sustainable forest management.

modelAnswer: The Himalayan Jungle Project helps conserve biodiversity by protecting Himalayan forests and the habitats of their wildlife.
It encourages local communities to take part in conservation and sustainable forest management.

items.followUp: Describe how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Award for stating that increasing CO₂ concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis when other factors are not limiting.
rubric.description: As CO₂ concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided other factors are not limiting.
rubric.how: Look for the rate rising as CO₂ concentration rises.

rubric.why: Award for stating that the rate eventually reaches a maximum or levels off when another factor limits photosynthesis.
rubric.description: The rate eventually reaches a maximum and levels off when another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Look for a maximum rate, levelling off, or a limiting factor.

modelAnswer: As CO₂ concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided other factors are not limiting.
The rate eventually reaches a maximum and levels off when another factor becomes limiting.
